old_pre_w3.prompt: An analyst retypes OKONO's inventory with every capex and the limit as a count of USD instead of million USD, and changes nothing else. What changes in how the engine solves it, and where would the analyst see the change?
options: Nothing changes in the solve, because risked EMV per million USD is a ratio whose unit cancels, so the ranking and the set come out identical.
The engine refuses the run with a PortfolioInputError, since a capex that large beside NPVs in million USD fails the engine's scale check.
The limit is no longer at most 5000, so the grid turns coarse at the limit divided by 2000 per cell, and only the reported resolution shows the switch.
The grid stays at 1 million USD per cell but every project now weighs a million times more cells, so none of them fits under the limit and nothing is funded at all.
old_pre_w3.explanation: The exact grid needs whole numbers and a limit of at most 5000; the published rawDollars case runs on a cell of 225000.000000 USD and still reaches the exact 250.0000, with a gap of 0.0000.

They broke a near tie, because the engine penalises each set's risked EMV by its simulated loss probability before comparing it with the rest of the frontier.
They screened the inventory, since any project whose failure branch lifts a set's P(loss) above the default is dropped before the knapsack runs.
They decided OK-3, which the simulation found worth its risk at 450.0000 and not worth it at 600.0000, where a safer set was available.
old_pre_w3.explanation: The 600.0000 set wins because 402.7500 beats every other set that fits, not because it is safer; a lower-risk set of nearly equal value is never offered.

old_pre_w3.prompt: A risky project's chance of success is left blank in an inventory. Beyond its risked EMV, what does the blank do to the seeded risk summary of a set that funds it?
options: Nothing, since the simulation draws its own success rate from the entered percentiles whatever pos says, and only the optimizer uses the default.
The default of 1 travels into the simulation, so the project succeeds in every iteration, never adds a failure to P(loss) and never drags down the P90.
The simulation refuses to run for that set and reports P(loss) as null until a chance of success is entered for every funded project.
The simulation treats the blank as a coin toss and draws success half the time, so the set looks riskier than its risked EMV would suggest.
old_pre_w3.explanation: A defaulted value is used everywhere the project is used; at seed 20260829 and 10000 iterations the project is a certain success, so one blank row makes a set look both more valuable and safer.

options: A separate simulation of B + C, because the engine's risk summary covers only the set it returned and its output names no alternative optimum.
Nothing extra, since the risk summary averages P(loss) over every set that ties on risked EMV and reports the blended figure beside the funded set.

new.prompt: Working a graded inventory, a candidate finds the result reports solveMethod "grid-feasible". What does the Associate method require before the funded set is quoted?
options: Nothing extra, since the fallback rounds every weight up and a set that fits its grid can only be the exact optimum.

questions.why: keyed answer false: progress above 100 percent is refused

old_pre_w3.prompt: Checking OFON-1's inputs before the AFE is read, an answer finds every progress at 0 or more. What must it still point out?
options: Nothing more, because the engine refuses progress outside 0 to 100 percent, exactly as its message says, so a report that returns metrics has passed both bounds of the check.
Any line at 0 percent, because the engine treats a line not yet begun as refused progress and drops its budget from planned value.
Any progress above 100 percent, which the engine accepts and which earns value beyond the budget, as the published case's CPI of 1.666667 shows.
Any line at 100 percent, such as CSG-02, because a complete line is clamped and its actual of 4300000 is taken out of CPI.
old_pre_w3.explanation: Negative progress throws AfeInputError, but only the lower bound is enforced; CSG-02 sits at 100.0000 percent with actuals of 4300000 against a budget of 3900000 and could be pushed past 100 with no refusal.
